drivingQuestion: Does the unsupervised slaughter of a deaf-mute, an imbecile or a minor count as an act of slaughter?
outcomeNote: A mishna: R׳ Meir and the Rabbis dispute the latter clause and the Rabbis concede on lashes; nothing is resolved here.

segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ חֵרֵשׁ שׁוֹטֶה וְקָטָן שֶׁשָּׁחֲטוּ, וַאֲחֵרִים רוֹאִין אוֹתָם – חַיָּיב לְכַסּוֹת. בֵּינָן לְבֵין עַצְמָן – פָּטוּר מִלְּכַסּוֹת.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» In the case of «a deaf-mute, an imbecile, or a minor who slaughtered» an undomesticated animal or a bird, «and others saw them» and ensured that the slaughter was properly performed, in which case the slaughter is valid (see 2a), one who oversaw the slaughter is «obligated to cover» the blood. If they slaughtered the animals «among themselves» without supervision, one is «exempt» from the obligation to cover the blood.

segments.he: וְכֵן לְעִנְיַן אוֹתוֹ וְאֶת בְּנוֹ, שֶׁשָּׁחֲטוּ וַאֲחֵרִים רוֹאִין אוֹתָן – אָסוּר לִשְׁחוֹט אַחֲרֵיהֶם, בֵּינָן לְבֵין עַצְמָן – רַבִּי מֵאִיר מַתִּיר לִשְׁחוֹט אַחֲרֵיהֶן, וַחֲכָמִים אוֹסְרִים, וּמוֹדִים שֶׁאִם שָׁחַט – שֶׁאֵינוֹ סוֹפֵג אֶת הָאַרְבָּעִים.
segments.en: «And likewise with regard to the matter of» slaughtering «a mother and its offspring» on the same day, if a deaf-mute, an imbecile, or a minor «slaughtered» an undomesticated mother animal «and others saw them,» it is «prohibited to slaughter» its offspring «after them.» If they slaughtered the mother animal «among themselves, Rabbi Meir deems» it «permitted to slaughter» its offspring «after them and the Rabbis deem» it «prohibited. And» the Rabbis «concede that if one slaughtered» the offspring thereafter «that he does not incur the forty» lashes, as it is possible the mother was not properly slaughtered.

moves.summary: the mishna rules that a supervised slaughter by them obligates covering the blood and an unsupervised one does not
the same distinction is applied to slaughtering a mother and its offspring on one day
moves.about: whether the unsupervised slaughter of a mother animal by a deaf-mute, an imbecile or a minor counts as an act of slaughter, so that its offspring may not be slaughtered the same day

moves.summary: R׳ Meir permits slaughtering the offspring after an unsupervised slaughter

moves.about: whether one who does slaughter the offspring after their unsupervised slaughter incurs the forty lashes

moves.summary: the Rabbis concede that one who did slaughter the offspring is not flogged
